title: Prime Pairs With Target Sum
summary: Given an integer n, find all pairs of prime numbers (x, y) such that x + y = n and x <= y <= n.
statement: Given an integer n, find all pairs of prime numbers (x, y) such that x + y = n and x <= y <= n. Return a sorted list of these pairs in ascending order by x. If no such pairs exist, return an empty list.
constraints: Find prime numbers x and y with x+y=n and x<=y.
List each unordered pair once in increasing x order.
Return an empty list when no pair exists.
hints: Build a primality sieve through n.
Check x only through n/2 so each unordered pair appears once.
Emit [x,n-x] when both entries are prime.
The bounded scan covers exactly one orientation of every possible sum pair, while the sieve gives correct primality.
editorial: The bounded scan covers exactly one orientation of every possible sum pair, while the sieve gives correct primality.

tests.explanation: Only 1+2 is possible, but one is not prime, so no pair exists.
